title: UNC men's basketball center Cameron Fens cleared to play after judge's ruling

 UNC men's basketball center Cameron Fens cleared to play after judge's ruling
 An Orange County judge granted UNC center Cameron Fens' request for a temporary restraining order, but his legal battle continues. Fens is temporarily cleared to play for the Tar Heels after missing the first four games of the season.

 By Ryan Bisesi, Shaun Gallagher and Brian Murphy, WRAL News
 The North Carolina men's basketball team is getting some long-awaited help in the frontcourt.
 UNC center Cameron Fens was granted a temporary restraining order Thursday in a ruling by Orange County Superior Court Judge Alyson Grine, which clears the way for the 7-foot center to take the floor for the Tar Heels, at least temporarily.
 Other WRAL Top Stories
 He is also seeking a preliminary injunction that would allow him to play while his lawsuit against the NCAA proceeds. A preliminary injunction hearing is scheduled for Nov. 30. Fens is eligible until a decision is made in that hearing or Dec. 1, whichever comes first.
 Fens, who has played four seasons of college basketball, sought an order prohibiting the NCAA and others from treating him as ineligible or penalizing North Carolina for allowing him to play. His complaint argued that he deserved an extra season due to a misdiagnosed foot injury during the 2024-25 season and because of new NCAA rules that allow future players to have five seasons of eligibility but exclude players, like Fens, who entered school for the 2022-23 season.
 Fens played two seasons at Illinois-Chicago and two at South Dakota before transferring to UNC. He averaged 14.4 points and 8.7 rebounds per game for South Dakota last season. Fens has yet to appear in a game for the Tar Heels as he has navigated a months-long legal battle over his eligibility. 
 Grine indicated in her ruling that Fens had a likelihood of success on both the injury and eligibility claims. She stated that nothing in the NCAA’s bylaws “indicates the amended rule only applies to students who have eligibility under the prior (four-in-five) rule.”
 Since late June, 220 lawsuits have been filed challenging eligibility rules. More than half of those are challenging the age-based or five-for-five rule. About half of the 850 players seeking eligibility for the 2026-27 academic year have been granted relief from the courts. 
 UNC football kicker Rece Verhoff and three members of the Tar Heels’ field hockey team gained an additional year of eligibility though court cases, as did former UNC basketball players Ven-Allen Lubin (NC State) and Seth Trimble (Louisville).
 “This is yet another example of how conflicting state court decisions are destabilizing college sports nationwide,” the NCAA said in a statement about the Fens’ case. “This particular individual is a plaintiff in a copycat lawsuit in Tennessee, in which an appellate court has already stayed a preliminary injunction because the plaintiffs were unlikely to succeed on the merits. Situations like these are exactly why we need Congress to pass the Protect College Sports Act to set nationwide standards and prevent unfairness from this kind of court-shopping from infecting college sports while also robbing future generations of student-athletes of roster spots and playing time.”
 With the season already underway, Fens' attorneys argued that immediate relief was necessary to prevent him from missing more games. 
 UNC coach Michael Malone said in an affidavit filed as part of the lawsuit that Fens would be part of the Tar Heels' regular rotation if eligible to play.
 The Tar Heels (3-1) host Marshall at 9 p.m. Friday at the Smith Center. UNC hasn’t said whether Fens will play in the game.
 In his affidavit, Malone mentioned several fifth-year players that are playing for teams that UNC will compete against this season, including Trimble, Lubin, West Virginia’s Brenen Lorient and Javan Buchanan, Syracuse’s Amarri Monroe, Wake Forest’s Justin Abson and Miami’s Malik Reneau.

 Cameron Fens, who transferred to UNC from South Dakota, is asking an Orange County judge to allow him to play for the Tar Heels this season. Fens has already played four seasons of college basketball.
